note: The drill library for /practice (issue #55). Every drill is random practice with a score: a new target, distance or lie on every ball, never the same shot twice in a row. Pass marks are hand-set starting points, not yet calibrated to handicap (docs/quality.md). Ranges are in the app's display units: yards off the green, feet on it. Checked by src/lib/practice/drills.test.ts.

drills.name: Approach ladder
drills.setup: Pick three targets spread across your focus range: a short, a middle and a long one. Give each a scoring zone about the size of a green (10 yards either side of the flag).
steps: Hit 9 balls, 3 at each target, in a random order: never the same target twice in a row.
Go through your full routine on every ball: pick the club, pick the line, commit.
A ball scores if it finishes inside the zone.
drills.rationale: On the course every approach is a new distance. Changing target on every ball makes you pick a club and commit each time, which is the skill the round asks for.

drills.name: Wedge distance matrix
drills.setup: Take three wedges and three swing lengths (for example half, three-quarter and full). Write down the carry you expect from each of the 9 combinations.
steps: Hit each club and length once, 9 shots, in a random order.
Call the number before you swing.
A shot scores if it carries within 5 yards of the number you called.
drills.rationale: Most shots inside 100 yards are lost to distance, not direction. Knowing your 9 numbers turns a guess into a stock shot.

drills.name: Circle putting, 4 to 8 ft
drills.setup: Put 4 tees around a hole at 4, 5, 6 and 8 feet, each on a different side so you get uphill, downhill and both breaks.
steps: Hit 20 putts, moving to a different tee after every putt.
Read each one fresh and go through your full routine.
drills.rationale: These are the putts a scratch golfer holes most of the time, so every miss is a stroke lost. Moving every putt makes each one a real read, like on the course.

drills.name: Lag putting, 30 to 50 ft
drills.setup: Pick three holes on the practice green and a spot 30, 40 and 50 feet from each.
steps: Hit 10 putts, changing both hole and distance after every putt.
Pace off each putt before you hit it.
A putt scores if it finishes within 3 feet of the hole, or drops.
drills.rationale: Three-putts come from the first putt, not the second. Leaving long putts inside 3 feet takes most of them away.

drills.name: Bunker to 10 ft
drills.setup: Use a greenside bunker with at least two holes to aim at.
steps: Hit 10 balls, changing the hole and your lie (flat, up, down, a bit buried) after every ball.
Rake and drop a fresh ball each time: no hitting from the same footprint.
A ball scores if it finishes within 10 feet of the hole.
drills.rationale: Most strokes lost from greenside bunkers come from leaving the ball too far away, or in the sand. Inside 10 feet you have a putt you can expect to hole.
